name: Security pack
description: Security for the whole project: code, auth, permissions, web and APIs, mobile, infrastructure, secrets and dependencies. LLM and MCP checks apply when relevant.
usage:
This is the project's general security pack. Before planning or changing code, identify the project's stack, assets, entry points, sensitive data and trust boundaries. Read `security-and-hardening` for security-sensitive work. Apply the relevant OWASP ASVS requirements and Cheat Sheet guidance: enforce server-side authorization for every resource, validate inputs, parameterize queries, protect credentials and personal data, use safe defaults and handle errors without leaking secrets. Use `sharp-edges` when designing APIs or configuration.

Choose reviews from the actual project surface, not from the fact that an AI agent is writing the code:
- All projects: `code-review-security` and `differential-review` for security-sensitive changes; `secrets-scan` before commit; `sca-audit` on resolved lockfiles before release and after dependency changes.
- Web applications: `web-security-review` for OWASP Top 10, authentication, sessions, access control, injection, browser protections and SSRF.
- HTTP APIs: `api-security-review` for ownership, tenant isolation, field-level permissions, unsafe consumption, replay and abuse limits.
- Mobile applications: `mobile-code-review` for platform permissions, secure storage, cryptography and network protections (OWASP MASVS/MASTG). Declare partial coverage when native code or runtime tests are unavailable, including cross-platform shells.
- Infrastructure as code: `iac-security-review` for Terraform/OpenTofu, Kubernetes/Helm and CloudFormation; review permissions, exposed resources, secret handling, encryption and deployment configuration.
- Only if the application implements LLM/RAG/agent functionality: `llm-risk-assess`. Treat prompts, retrieved documents and model output as untrusted; enforce authorization outside the model and bound tokens, time, cost and resource usage.
- Only if the project implements or configures MCP servers/tools: `mcp-server-review`. Minimize capabilities, validate inputs and outputs, and check data exposure. Using an AI coding assistant alone does not make the project an AI application.

Test denied access, cross-user/cross-tenant access and malformed input, plus abuse, replay and resource limits where relevant. Never print secret values or validate live credentials; redact findings and recommend revocation/rotation if exposed. Run scanners and attack probes only against the authorized local/test scope; do not upload code or secrets to external services.

OWASP skills may reference plugin files that the skills CLI does not copy. Read missing `plays/<file>.md` and `templates/finding.md` from https://github.com/OWASP/secure-agent-playbook/tree/main/plugins/code-security-skills or, for LLM/MCP reviews, https://github.com/OWASP/secure-agent-playbook/tree/main/plugins/ai-security-skills. The web review uses `plays/owasp-top10-web-review.md`. ASVS, MASVS, MASTG and infrastructure reference files are under https://github.com/OWASP/secure-agent-playbook/tree/main/plugins/code-security-skills/data (preserve the skill's `data/<dataset>/<file>` path). Official standards and prevention guidance: https://owasp.org/ASVS/, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/, https://mas.owasp.org/ and https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/. Check the cited edition: some plays use Top 10:2021 category numbers; do not relabel those as Top 10:2025.

Report reviewed scope, applicable and non-applicable checks with reasons, file:line evidence, severity, fixes, tests and scanner results, and anything not checked. If a skill, reference or scanner is unavailable, say so explicitly and do not claim that check passed. Skills guide the agent; installation, a clean scan or this pack is not proof of security, ASVS compliance or certification.

usage: Review package name, exports/bin/files, license and npm pack --dry-run output before publishing. Use npm trusted publishing or a scoped token in CI; publishing requires explicit release authorization. In a workspace whose root is private, pack and publish the intended packages/<name> directory, not the repository root.
setupTasks: npm: reserve the package name, configure trusted publishing and review the package contents before the first release.

name: GitHub Releases
description: Versioned desktop apps and binary release artifacts.
usage: Build artifacts for each supported OS/architecture, sign/notarize where required and upload to a reviewed GitHub Release. Never ship development credentials or unsigned automatic update manifests.
setupTasks: Configure per-platform builds, signing/notarization and a release workflow before distributing binaries.

name: Chrome Web Store
description: Publish browser extension packages to the Chrome Web Store.
usage: Build the extension, review permissions/host access and package the production extension output. Store credentials belong in the CI secret store; publication needs a store account and review.
setupTasks: Create the store listing, prepare privacy/permission disclosures and review the release package before submission.

name: VS Code Marketplace
description: Package and publish VS Code extensions.
usage: Review the extension manifest and permissions, package with @vscode/vsce and test the VSIX before publishing. Keep publisher credentials in CI secrets.
setupTasks: Create the publisher, review vsce package output and configure Marketplace publishing credentials.

name: GitHub Actions
description: Frontend/workspace CI with explicit service setup tasks.
usage: The workflow builds the JavaScript workspace or frontend directory. Add separate backend jobs with the correct Python/Ruby/Java/Go toolchain and the kit verification command before treating CI as full coverage. Do not install frontend dependencies in the repository root.

writeFiles.content:
name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10
      - name: Check workspace
        run: |
          if [ -f pnpm-workspace.yaml ]; then
            pnpm install
            pnpm run --if-present build
            pnpm run --if-present test
          elif [ -f package.json ]; then
            npm install
            npm run --if-present build
            npm run --if-present test
          fi
          if [ -f frontend/package.json ]; then
            cd frontend
            npm install
            npm run build
          fi

setupTasks: Add backend verification jobs matching the kit verify command and service roots before relying on CI.

name: Per-service deployment
description: Independent deployment roots for the frontend and backend services.
usage: Deploy each application from its actual root (frontend/backend, or the relevant apps/ directory). Configure each service build/start command, secrets, public URL and allowed origins separately; never publish the whole monorepo as one static site.
setupTasks: Connect each service to its deployment provider and configure its repository root and environment variables.

name: Workspace tests
description: Use the test/build targets already provided by every workspace service.
usage: Run the kit verification command across all service roots. Keep frontend and backend test tools in their own packages/virtual environments, with integration tests for API contracts. No extra packages are installed at the monorepo root.

name: Service quality checks
description: Review and automate quality checks within each service root.
usage: Use the formatter, linter and typechecker appropriate to each service language. Add commands in each service and aggregate them in CI; avoid a root dependency installation that hides missing frontend/backend dependencies.

name: Shouldly
description: Shouldly for ASP.NET Core projects.
usage: Use expressive assertions in the existing xUnit tests and test behavior at the application boundary.

name: MailKit
description: MailKit for ASP.NET Core projects.
usage: Create the SMTP client on demand with explicit TLS, authentication and timeouts; keep credentials in server environment variables and never connect during application startup.

name: ASP.NET localization
description: Localization middleware and resources included in ASP.NET Core.
usage: Register localization and request-localization middleware, declare supported cultures and put messages in resource files. No extra package is required.

name: Sign in with Apple
description: AuthenticationServices and Sign in with Apple from the iOS SDK.
usage: Configure the Sign in with Apple capability and use AuthenticationServices. Verify identity tokens/nonces on a trusted server and authorize resources separately. No extra package is required.

name: OSLog
description: Structured logging with the Apple OSLog framework.
usage: Use Logger with subsystem/category and privacy-aware interpolation. Do not log tokens, identifiers or personal data as public. No extra package is required.

name: StoreKit
description: In-app subscriptions and purchases through StoreKit.
usage: Use StoreKit 2 and verified transactions. Keep entitlement decisions server-backed when needed, finish processed transactions and test purchases with a local StoreKit configuration before release. No extra package is required.

name: StateFlow + ViewModel
description: State management using the Kotlin/Android primitives in the template.
usage: Expose immutable StateFlow from lifecycle-scoped ViewModels and collect it with lifecycle awareness in Compose. Keep mutable state private and model loading/error states explicitly.

name: Android resources
description: Localized strings and plurals using the Android resource system.
usage: Use values/strings.xml and locale-specific values-* directories, stringResource/pluralStringResource and locale-aware formatting. Keep secrets and server messages out of resource strings. No extra package is required.

name: Room
description: Android SQLite persistence with Room.
usage: The Room runtime is added to the Android app module. Configure the Room compiler with the Kotlin-compatible KSP plugin before defining entities/DAOs; use transactional migrations and never store credentials in plain SQLite.
setupTasks: Configure the Room compiler/KSP plugin matching the project Kotlin version and add database migrations before using DAOs.

name: Sentry
description: Official Angular error and tracing SDK.
usage: Configure the Angular ErrorHandler integration and optional tracing provider. Leave DSN unset until configured, redact credentials and keep sendDefaultPii false.
setupTasks: Configure the official Angular SDK providers and a DSN before reporting errors.

name: Angular localization
description: Angular message extraction and localized builds.
usage: Configure @angular/localize with ng add @angular/localize, mark templates/messages for translation and define source/target locales in angular.json. Keep runtime locale changes separate from localized build configuration.
setupTasks: Run the Angular localization schematic and configure supported locales and translation files.

name: Angular unit tests
description: The unit test runner configured by the official Angular CLI.
usage: Use the generated ng test target, with --watch=false in CI. Keep component tests focused on rendered behavior and cover services/auth failures. No extra package is installed beyond the official template.

name: Bun Test
description: The TypeScript test runner included in Bun.
usage: Write tests with bun:test and run bun test. Exercise Elysia handlers with app.handle(new Request(...)) without opening a port. Separate application construction from listen(); cover validation failures and denied access. No additional package is installed.

name: Railway
description: Deploy a Bun server from a repository.
usage: Connect the repository to Railway, select Bun, install with bun install --frozen-lockfile and start the actual server entry point with bun run src/index.ts (or the project production script). Bind to 0.0.0.0 and Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000). Verify the runtime and health check before publishing.
setupTasks: Railway/Bun: configure the runtime, start command, PORT binding, health check and secrets in the service. This option does not create or publish an external service.

name: Spring Boot Test
description: JUnit and Spring test support from the official starter.
usage: The base kit includes spring-boot-starter-test. Run ./mvnw test; use focused MVC/repository test slices and reserve full @SpringBootTest contexts for integration checks. Cover authorization and invalid requests. No duplicate starter is added.

name: Spring Boot Actuator
description: Health and metrics from the actuator starter included in the kit.
usage: The base kit includes spring-boot-starter-actuator. Configure readiness/liveness and metrics for the actual deployment; expose only required endpoints and authorize sensitive management endpoints. Never expose env, heap dumps or configuration to unauthenticated users.

name: Laravel Pint
description: Laravel formatter included by the official application template.
usage: Run ./vendor/bin/pint --test in CI and ./vendor/bin/pint to format locally. The Laravel template already includes laravel/pint as a development dependency; do not install a second formatter.

name: OpenAPI contract
description: Start a design-first OpenAPI document and validate changes with Redocly CLI.
usage: Describe endpoints in api/openapi.json before implementing them. From the service directory, validate the contract with `npx --yes @redocly/cli@2 lint --extends spec api/openapi.json`.

name: NestJS Swagger UI
description: Generate interactive API documentation and an OpenAPI JSON document from NestJS controllers.
usage: Run the API and open /docs for Swagger UI or /docs-json for its contract. Document request and response DTOs using @nestjs/swagger decorators.

writeFiles.content: import { DocumentBuilder, SwaggerModule } from '@nestjs/swagger';

const config = new DocumentBuilder().setTitle('{{name}} API').setVersion('1.0').build();
  SwaggerModule.setup('docs', app, () => SwaggerModule.createDocument(app, config));
